newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Gresik to tender for power supply.
newsitem.headline: Gresik to tender for power supply.

text.p: Indonesia's largest cement producer PT Semen Gresik said on Tuesday it will hold a tender to operate its 50-megawatt power plant to supply electricity to its Tonasa-IV plant in south Sulawesi following technical problems.

"Currently, we are operating only at 15 megawatts capacity due to the technical problems rather than the full utilisation rate of 50 megawatts," Muharram, a Semen Gresik official, told reporters after an analysts' briefing
He said Tonasa-IV's utilisation rate was at 58 percent of its total capacity in December but he did not disclose details.

Muharram said Semen Gresik expected either state-owned elecricity firm Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN) or the current contractor to manage the power plant, adding the result of the tender was expected to be known by March.
He said the current contractor is a firm from China but declined to name it.
Muharram said the contractor was working on the problems, which it expected to resolve by the middle of this year.
Semen Gresik is expected to supplement power for the Tonasa IV plant with electricity from PLN and power generators rented from other firms.
Muharram said the firm did not see any change in its cement production in 1997 despite the technical problems.
He said additional electricity supplies would be sufficient to allow Tonasa IV to have a utilisation rate of 60 to 70 percent until repairs were completed.
Muharram said Semen Gresik projected consolidated sales volume of 10.96 million tonnes in 1997, against 8.9 million tonnes in 1996. --Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
